links.comparator_used: single pooled model trained on all patients without race-specific training
links.outcome: Racial bias in error rates (FPR/FNR) for predicting uncontrolled hypertension (SBP >160 mmHg)
links.effect: Black patients had a 4.7x higher FPR and a 0.58x lower FNR than White patients; the authors conclude race-specific models were not sufficient to resolve the bias. No numeric results for the race-specific models are given in the abstract.
links.quote: Race-specific models are not sufficient to resolve such biases and require further decision threshold tuning.

links.comparator_used: a single common decision threshold applied to both Black and White patients
links.outcome: Equalizing false negative rate between Black and White patients
links.effect: Decision threshold differentiation was implemented to equalize FNR; no numeric post-adjustment values are reported in the abstract.
links.quote: Decision threshold differentiation was implemented to equalize FNR.

design_hint: Group-specific decision threshold tuning to equalize error rates
